Halloween became popular here in the netherlands during corona but is now less popular

It's interesting here (in Turkey), because we are a Muslim country but we have non-official celebrations similar to European holidays, even if they are a bit different. There's Cadılar Bayramı (Celebration of the Witches) which is basically like Halloween. There is also New Year Day (which is official), where people decorate trees like Christmas trees and there's even some santa stuff. Of course all of this is stripped from Christianity and totally secular.

What I said only applies to western regions of Turkey though. In the eastern regions, no such thing exists.

Yes, but I'm not sure. I heard something like that before, about Arabs in South America who were labelled "El Turco" because they had Ottoman passports.

Ottoman Empire was very diverse and had many ethnicities, and Ottoman empire officially never called itself "Turkish", rather it was called being an Ottoman citizen. But other countries just labelled all Ottoman citizens as Turks.

Even today, modern Turkey is very diverse ethnically. Turks, Kurds, Circassians, Laz, etc. I myself am not Turkish, but Circassian. We had to come to Turkey 150 years ago, but we still have our own different culture and language.
